verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Unfolding `physicalVelocity` gives exactly the four formulas, with the Lean's coordinate indices 0,1,2 for the paper's x_1,x_2,x_3. Angular coefficient: lift (swirlProfile) = q^{-A-1/2} F, and componentX/componentY put it as -x_1 * (q^{-A-1/2}F) in the first slot and +x_0 * (q^{-A-1/2}F) in the second, matching the paper's signs. Radial coefficient: B = radialB (fluxProfile) = -V_0/(2s) with s = qX and V_0 = X v_0, so -B = v_0/(2q) and -(x_i B) = (v_0/2q) x_i. Axial: lift (axialProfile) = q^{-A} U. Pressure: AxisymmetricResidual.pressure (pressureProfile) = q^{-2A} Π. The only rewriting is the elimination of s in favour of q and X in B. The repository also carries a second, equivalent encoding of the same field as a Cartesian curl of two potentials (`AxisymmetricFields.velocity`, used by `SlowBorelBase.baseVelocity`), whose component identities have the same shape; I did not verify in Lean that its two partial derivatives reduce to v_0/(2q) and -q^{-A-1/2}F.
